record.paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
record.original_question: Let {b1,...,bn} be a basis of C^n. Suppose F is entire on C^n and has bounded L-index in each basis direction bi, with L belonging to the corresponding class Q_bi^n for each i. Must F then have bounded L-index in every nonzero direction b that is a complex linear combination b = lambda1 b1 + ... + lambdan bn?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$. For a nonzero direction $\mathbf{b} \in \mathbb{C}^n \setminus \{0\}$, let $\mathcal{Q}_{\mathbf{b}}^n$ denote the class of positive continuous functions $L : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{R}_{+}$ satisfying

$$0 < \lambda_1(\mathbf{b}, \eta) := \inf_{z \in \mathbb{C}^n} \inf_{|t_1|, |t_2| \le \eta/L(z)} \frac{L(z + t_1 \mathbf{b})}{L(z + t_2 \mathbf{b})} \le \sup_{z \in \mathbb{C}^n} \sup_{|t_1|, |t_2| \le \eta/L(z)} \frac{L(z + t_1 \mathbf{b})}{L(z + t_2 \mathbf{b})} =: \lambda_2(\mathbf{b}, \eta) < \infty$$

for every $\eta > 0$.

An entire function $F : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ if there exists a nonnegative integer $m$ such that for every $z \in \mathbb{C}^n$,

$$\frac{|\partial^k_{\mathbf{b}} F(z)|}{k!\, L(z)^k} \le \max_{0 \le j \le m} \frac{|\partial^j_{\mathbf{b}} F(z)|}{j!\, L(z)^j} \qquad \text{for all } k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0},$$

where $\partial_{\mathbf{b}} F(z) = \sum_{j=1}^{n} b_j \frac{\partial F}{\partial z_j}(z)$ is the directional derivative.

Let $\{\mathbf{b}_1, \dots, \mathbf{b}_n\}$ be a basis of $\mathbb{C}^n$, and for each $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$ let $L_i \in \mathcal{Q}_{\mathbf{b}_i}^n$. Suppose $F$ is an entire function on $\mathbb{C}^n$ that has bounded $L_i$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}_i$ for every $i = 1, \dots, n$.

Question: Must $F$ have bounded $L$-index in every nonzero direction $\mathbf{b} = \lambda_1 \mathbf{b}_1 + \cdots + \lambda_n \mathbf{b}_n$ (with $\lambda_i \in \mathbb{C}$ not all zero), for some appropriate choice of $L \in \mathcal{Q}_{\mathbf{b}}^n$?
artifact.category_tag: Entire functions of bounded L-index in direction
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned several papers on slice holomorphic and entire functions of bounded L-index in a direction, but no source directly stating that the question of whether boundedness of L-index along the directions of a basis implies boundedness of L-index along all directions has been resolved. The status appears to remain undetermined in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Slice Holomorphic Functions in Several Variables with Bounded L-Index in Direction
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style discussion of properties of entire and slice holomorphic functions of bounded L-index in a direction, without claiming a resolution of the basis-versus-arbitrary-direction question.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to study bounded L-index in direction but does not appear to settle the basis-implies-arbitrary-direction problem.

status_evidence.title: Some criteria of boundedness of the L-index in direction for slice holomorphic functions
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes criteria for boundedness of L-index in a single fixed direction, leaving open issues comparing different directions.
status_evidence.claim: Existing criteria address one direction at a time and do not give an affirmative answer to the basis question.
